validity.recommendation: no action — existence, classification and phase-structure all confirmed
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: extremely well documented, well beyond the GEM-only-entity risk this sweep is calibrated to catch. Independent, non-GEM sources confirming the pipeline physically exists and is operating: Reuters (2021, FERC show-cause order over a $40M civil penalty for drilling-mud spills during Rover's own HDD construction), PBS NewsHour (2017, drilling-fluid wetland spill), DeSmog (2017, historic Stoneman House demolition dispute in Dennison OH), Livingston Daily and MLive (2017, Michigan protests against the pipeline), Grist (2019, construction/spill timeline), and the commercial pipeline database Rextag (confirms route, owners, operator). This is one of the most litigated/reported Appalachian gas pipelines in the tracker — no existence concern. CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate FERC-jurisdictional natural-gas TRANSMISSION pipeline (FERC Docket CP15-93, per the Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Ongoing Projects' industry report, Oct/Nov 2018 ed., which lists Energy Transfer Partners/Rover Pipeline LLC under Docket CP15-93) — not a gathering or process line. Status='operating' and Fuel='Gas' both confirmed (PBS: 'will transport up to 3.25 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day'; Grist: system 'became fully operational late last year' [2018], referring to the full 2-phase system). DUPLICATE/PHASE STRUCTURE: per the batch's own calibration this is one of 4 Rover rows (P0392 Phase 1, P2438 Phase 2, P2604 Rover Expansion, P2635 Wick Meter Station Expansion) that are legitimate additive scopes of one ~3.25 Bcf/d system, not duplicates. Verified the math independently: P0392's Capacity (1700 MMcf/d) + P2438's Capacity (1550 MMcf/d) = 3250 MMcf/d = 3.25 Bcf/d, matching the SYSTEM total independently reported by PBS (3.25 Bcf/d) and the PGJ report (3.25 Bcf/d, Docket CP15-93). This is strong corroboration that the two-phase split in GEM is correct and internally consistent, even though (per the aggregate-vs-segment rule) the system total is never itself a ref for either phase row individually. Opened 9 of the wiki page's 13 harvested citations (PGJ Ongoing Projects PDF, PBS, Grist, DeSmog, Livingston Daily, MLive [wayback], Reuters [wayback], Rextag, roverpipelinefacts.com); FracTracker and the bare EIA data portal were opened but did not name 'Rover' on the page (generic aggregator/portal pages, not usable per the relevance rule); the ir.energytransfer.com press-release link (Aug 2017 Phase 1A FERC in-service announcement) is dead — connection timeout, no Wayback snapshot found either — flagging as broken but NOT a deletion signal, since the pipeline's existence and 2017 in-service milestone are independently corroborated elsewhere; the roverpipelinefacts.com PDF link (final-laterals announcement) 404s.

validity.recommendation: attach refs; construction year is well corroborated, start year only medium-tier
validity.researcher_notes: ConstructionYear=2017: HIGH tier, 3 independent sources agree construction was underway in 2017 — Reuters ('In April 2017, shortly after Rover began its HDD operation...' — FERC-sourced fact, independent of GEM/ET), Grist ('Construction began in March 2017'), PBS ('scheduled completion mid-2017', article published ~April 2017 describing active construction). StartYear1=2017 (Phase 1 in-service): MEDIUM tier — the PGJ industry report (Energy Transfer-sourced, so not independent of the operator) states 'Status: Phase 1A of the pipeline is in-service and construction has started on Phase II' with 'Completion: 4Q 2017'. Reuters (independent) notes the project 'was initially planned to be completed in November 2017' but was delayed by the spill/violations litigation — this is consistent with, not contradictory to, a 2017 StartYear (Phase 1A went into partial service Aug 31, 2017 per the wiki's cited Energy Transfer press release headline, though that URL itself is now dead — see existence note). Searched for a second fully-independent source stating the exact in-service year; PBS/Grist/DeSmog/Livingston Daily/MLive cover construction and controversy but none states an explicit in-service date for Phase 1 specifically. Recording as medium tier and flagging that a second independent source for the precise Phase 1 in-service year is still owed.

validity.researcher_notes: Owner1/2/3 = Energy Transfer 32.57% / Blackstone 32.44% / Traverse 35.00%. Rextag (independent commercial pipeline database) states: 'Owned by Energy Transfer/Blackstone and Traverse' and separately 'Energy Transfer (50.1%) / Blackstone (49.9%) holds 65% stake; Traverse holds 35% stake.' The math checks out almost exactly against the sheet: 65% x 50.1% = 32.565% (sheet: 32.57%), 65% x 49.9% = 32.435% (sheet: 32.44%), and Traverse's 35% matches exactly. This is a real, well-known 2018 transaction (ArcLight-backed Traverse Midstream Partners bought a 35% stake in Rover from Energy Transfer/Blackstone) but I could only corroborate it with the one independent source (Rextag) inside the time available — searched news wire coverage of the Traverse Midstream transaction for a second source and could not complete that search (web-search budget for this session was exhausted mid-task; only direct URL fetches were available afterward). Flagging tier=medium and the second-source search as still owed, not abandoned.

validity.recommendation: attach caveat ref; a phase-specific independent length source is still owed
validity.researcher_notes: LengthKnown=711 mi. The only length figure found for the Rover system is in the PGJ 'Ongoing Projects' industry report (Oct/Nov 2018 ed.): 'Length: 713 miles' under the overall 'Rover Pipeline' project entry (Docket CP15-93, Energy Transfer Partners-sourced data) — a SYSTEM total (both phases, 'two dual mainlines'), not phase-specific, and not independent of the operator (same origin as roverpipelinefacts.com). 711 vs 713 is a trivial (0.3%) difference and not a material conflict, but per the aggregate-vs-segment rule this system figure cannot properly serve as Phase 1's ref. Rextag (independent) states a very different figure — '1,144-mile pipeline' — for the whole Rover system, but this almost certainly reflects a different counting convention (Rover's mainline runs as twin 42-inch parallel pipes ['Mainline A' and 'Mainline B'] plus 8 supply laterals; summing both mainline strings plus all laterals would roughly explain the gap from a single-route-mile figure like 711/713). I did not find a source that states a Phase-1-specific length independent of the operator. No material disagreement found (Rextag's bigger number reflects a different definition of 'length', not a competing claim about Phase 1's route miles), so this stays a caveat rather than a concern, but the caveat is real: nothing independent nails 711 specifically to Phase 1.

Diameter=42 in. PGJ 'Ongoing Projects' report lists the Rover mainline segment ('Mainlines A and B') at 42 inches, consistent with the sheet. This is the only source found stating a diameter explicitly, and it is Energy Transfer-sourced (not independent). Searched DeSmog/PBS/Grist/Livingston Daily/MLive/Reuters/Rextag — none states pipe diameter. Recording at medium tier; a second, independent source for diameter is still owed.

validity.recommendation: attach ref; capacity is corroborated indirectly via the additive system total, not directly per-phase
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=1700 MMcf/d (Phase 1). No source states 1700 MMcf/d specifically for Phase 1 alone. But the SYSTEM total of 3.25 Bcf/d (3250 MMcf/d) is independently confirmed by PBS ('will transport up to 3.25 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day') and the PGJ report ('Capacity: 3.25 Bcf/d'), and 1700 (this row) + 1550 (P2438, Phase 2) = 3250 MMcf/d exactly — internally consistent with the well-corroborated system total. Recording at medium tier given the phase-level figure itself isn't independently sourced, only the arithmetic-consistent total.

validity.recommendation: verify SegmentCost against a documented Phase-1-specific capitalized cost — do not simply overwrite with the $4.2B system total (aggregate-vs-segment rule)
validity.researcher_notes: SegmentCost=$3,000,000,000 (Phase 1). This does not match ANY source found. Two independent sources — PBS and Grist — both state the Rover Pipeline PROJECT cost as '$4.2 billion' (a widely and consistently reported figure, also repeated by the PGJ industry report, though PGJ is operator-sourced). Nothing found gives a Phase-1-only cost breakdown, so per the aggregate-vs-segment rule the well-corroborated $4.2B figure cannot simply replace the current $3B (that's the whole-project/whole-system figure, not Phase 1's share). But the current $3B value itself is unsupported by anything I found — it doesn't match the $4.2B total, and no source splits the cost by phase to justify a $3B Phase-1-specific figure either. Flagging as a genuine spec concern: the current value is unconfirmed and likely stale/wrong, but I'm not proposing a replacement number since doing so would risk the same aggregate-vs-segment error the sheet may already have made. Whoever resolves this should look for a phase-specific capitalized-cost disclosure (Energy Transfer 10-K/investor materials) rather than defaulting to the system total.

Searched all 13 harvested wiki citations plus direct fetches of PBS, Grist, DeSmog, Livingston Daily, MLive, Reuters, Rextag, roverpipelinefacts.com, and the PGJ industry report — none states an explicit proposal/announcement year. The FERC docket number itself (CP15-93) is suggestive under FERC's standard 2-digit-year-of-filing convention (implying an application filed in 2015), but that is an inference from a numbering convention, not an explicit sourced statement, so I'm not staging it as a value. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a year from the docket number alone; a second pass with a working web-search budget could likely resolve this (Rover's 2014 open-season announcement / 2015 FERC application are publicly documented but I could not locate a citable page in the time available).

No source in the harvested citation pool or found via direct search states an operating/MAOP pressure for Rover Pipeline. This would most likely require the FERC certificate order itself (elibrary.ferc.gov, Docket CP15-93) or a PHMSA filing, neither of which I could pull into readable text in the time available (eLibrary is a JS-driven search app that doesn't yield document text via a plain HTTP fetch, and this session's web-search budget was exhausted before I could locate the exact order PDF path). Leaving UNRESOLVED.

cross_row_leads.facts: As of this Oct/Nov 2018 industry report: 'Status: Phase 1A of the pipeline is in-service and construction has started on Phase II of the project' (as of the underlying Oct 2017 revision date on the entry) — corroborates P2438 (Rover Phase 2) as a genuine, real construction phase, not a duplicate of Phase 1. Also: P0392's Capacity (1700) + P2438's Capacity (1550) = 3250 MMcf/d, matching this report's system-wide 'Capacity: 3.25 Bcf/d' and PBS's independently reported 'up to 3.25 billion cubic feet' — strong corroboration that the phase split and both phases' capacity figures are internally consistent.

summary: P0392 (Rover Pipeline, Phase 1) is a real, extremely well-documented FERC-jurisdictional (CP15-93) interstate gas transmission line, correctly classified, correctly split from Phase 2 (P2438) as an additive system (capacities sum exactly to the independently-corroborated 3.25 Bcf/d total) — no existence/classification/duplicate concern. One spec concern: SegmentCost ($3B) matches no source found; independent reporting (PBS, Grist) gives $4.2B for the whole project/system, which can't simply replace a phase-level figure. Length, Diameter, Capacity, Owner-percentages and StartYear1 are confirmed only with caveats (single-source or operator-affiliated; a second independent source is owed for each). Operator ('Rover Pipeline LLC') filled at high tier (2 independent sources). ProposalYear/Month and Pressure are UNRESOLVED — nothing in the harvested pool or direct search states either.
